 &\qquad\qquad\cdot
 \sum_{a\in(O_{\mathfrak l}/\mathfrak l^nO_{\mathfrak l})^\times}
 \theta^\sigma\psi(aa_i g^{-1})
 \Upsilon_{i}\left(
   \frac{a}{\varpi_{\mathfrak l}^n}
 \right)\cap\eta_{f,i}
 \equiv0\pmod{\mathfrak P}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Here, the symbols are taken at level $\mathfrak N$.
Proposition~\ref{prop:average:lpower:l} shows that the common support of
the inner sums in \eqref{eq:proof-prop106-character-average} is
\[
 i=1,\qquad
 a=\varepsilon g \gamma\in E_Fg\Gamma_{n-n_0}/\Gamma_n.
\]
The character $\theta$ is trivial on $E_F$, and the automorphic symbols are $E_F$-invariant by
Lemma~\ref{lem:unit-action-automorphic-symbol}. Hence the terms indexed
by $\varepsilon g\gamma$ do not depend on $\varepsilon$.
Writing $\gamma=1+\varpi_{\mathfrak l}^{n-n_0}b$, the resulting
identity is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:proof-prop106-two-additive-sums}
 \#E_F\sum_{b\ {\rm mod}\ \mathfrak l^{n_0}}
 \mathbf e_F\left(
   \frac{bc_\theta}{\varpi_{\mathfrak l}^{n_0}}
 \right)
 \Upsilon_{1}\left(
   \frac{g(1+\varpi_{\mathfrak l}^{n-n_0}b)}
        {\varpi_{\mathfrak l}^{n}}
 \right)\cap\eta_{f,1}
 \equiv0\pmod{\mathfrak P}.
\end{equation}

Put $u:=g/\varpi_{\mathfrak l}^{n}$ and $v_b:=b/\varpi_{\mathfrak l}^{n_0}$.
Using the equality $c_{\phi^\varepsilon}\equiv \varepsilon c_\phi \pmod{\mathfrak l^{n_0}}$,
taking change of variable $b\mapsto (\varepsilon g_0)^{-1} b$,
and summing \eqref{eq:proof-prop106-two-additive-sums} over
\(\theta=\phi^\varepsilon\), indexed by \(\varepsilon\in E_F\), we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:proof-prop106-level-composition}
 \#E_F\sum_{\varepsilon\in E_F}\sum_{b}
 \mathbf e_F\left(
   \frac{bc_\phi g_0^{-1}}{\varpi_{\mathfrak l}^{n_0}}
 \right)
 \mathrm{Tr}_E\Delta_1^*\alpha^*_{u+\varepsilon v_b,1}\eta_{f,1,\mathrm{c}}
 \equiv0\pmod{\mathfrak P}.
\end{equation}
Here, the underlying maps are
\[
 \alpha_{v_b,1}:Y^1(\mathfrak N')\longrightarrow
 Y_1^1(\mathfrak N),
 \qquad
 \alpha_{u,1}:Y^1(\mathfrak N\cap\mathfrak l^{2n})\longrightarrow
 Y_1^1(\mathfrak N').
\]
Note that we can choose matrices satisfying
$\alpha_{u+\varepsilon v_b,1}
=\alpha_{\varepsilon v_b,1}\alpha_{u,1}$
for every $b$ and $\varepsilon\in E_F$.

Let $\eta'$ be a compactly supported lift of $\eta_{f,1}$.
Since $\mathcal E_q$ commutes with the level-changing pullbacks at
$\mathfrak l$ and $\alpha_{v,1}^*\eta'=(\alpha_{v,1}^*\eta)'$
by the naturality, we have
\begin{align*}
\alpha_{u,1}^*(\mathcal F_{h,1}\eta_{f,1})_{\mathrm c}
&=\alpha_{u,1}^*\mathcal E_q
\left(
\sum_{b\ \mathrm{mod}\ \mathfrak l^{n_0}}
\mathbf e_F\left(\frac{bh}{\varpi_{\mathfrak l}^{n_0}}\right)
\sum_{\varepsilon\in E_F}
\alpha_{\varepsilon v_b,1}^*\eta'
\right)\\
&=\sum_{b}
\mathbf e_F\left(\frac{bh}{\varpi_{\mathfrak l}^{n_0}}\right)
\sum_{\varepsilon\in E_F}
\alpha_{u+\varepsilon v_b,1}^*\eta_{f,1,\mathrm c}
\end{align*}
for $h\in O_{\mathfrak l}^\times$.
Taking $h=c_\phi g_0^{-1}$, we conclude that
\eqref{eq:proof-prop106-level-composition} is equal to
\begin{equation*}                                             
 \#E_F\operatorname{Tr}_E\Delta_1^*\alpha_{u,1}^*
 (\mathcal F_{c_\phi g_0^{-1},1}\eta_{f,1})_{\mathrm c}
 \equiv0\pmod{\mathfrak P}.
\end{equation*}
Then the assertion follows from the definition of automorphic symbol.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:mod-p-nonvanishing}
Assume that $\mathfrak q$ is coprime to $\mathfrak J$.
Then, for every $\phi\in X^\circ$, there exist
$\varepsilon\in E_F$ and $\psi\in\widehat\Delta$ such that
\[
 L_f(\phi^\varepsilon\psi)
 \not\equiv0\pmod{\mathfrak P}.
\]
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Fix $\phi\in X^\circ$. Then $\phi\in X_n$ for some $n\in\mathfrak V$.
Assume the contrary, i.e.,
\[
L_f(\phi^\varepsilon\psi)\equiv0\pmod{\mathfrak P}
\qquad(\varepsilon\in E_F,\ \psi\in\widehat\Delta).
\]
Fix $g_0\in O_{\mathfrak l}^\times$.
Proposition~\ref{prop:first-averaged-congruence} gives
\[
\Upsilon_1\left(\frac{g}{\varpi_{\mathfrak l}^n}\right)
\cap
\mathcal F_{c_\phi g_0^{-1},1}\eta_{f,1}\equiv 0\pmod{\mathfrak P}
\]
for any $g\in g_0\Gamma_{n_0}/\Gamma_n$. Thus the naturality of the pairing,
Lemma~\ref{dualmap:isom} for $A=k'$ and 
Theorem~\ref{prop:vertical-full-rank-finite-field} imply
\[
\mathcal F_{c_\phi g_0^{-1},1}\eta_{f,1}\equiv 0\pmod{\mathfrak P}
\]
for every $g_0\in O_{\mathfrak l}^\times$.
This contradicts Proposition~\ref{prop:residual-nonvanishing-eta-f}.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:galois-average-reduction}, which is essential to the
proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:mod-p-nonvanishing}, requires the $\mathfrak p$-dependent bound on $n_0$.
On the other hand, our main theorem needs the assumption $\mathfrak p\nmid\mathfrak J$,
where \(\mathfrak J\) depends on \(n_0\).
If \(n_0\) were chosen for each \(\mathfrak p\), then
\(\mathfrak J\) would also vary with \(\mathfrak p\), 
making the condition $\mathfrak p\nmid\mathfrak J$ in the statement of 
Theorem~\ref{thm:mod-p-nonvanishing} circular.
The set $P_h$ with cutoff \(h>h_0\) removes this circular dependence:
\(\mathcal P_h\) has positive density, and then fix \(n_0\geq h\). 
Thus Lemma~\ref{lem:galois-average-reduction} applies uniformly to every
\(\mathfrak p\in P_h\), while \(\mathfrak J\) is fixed independently
of \(\mathfrak p\).
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
\label{rem:positive:density}
Let $\mathfrak p\in \mathcal P_h$.
Our main theorem is true for any $\mathfrak P$ lying above $\mathfrak p$
satisfying $B\cap\mathfrak P\nmid\mathfrak J$.
Note that the density of $\mathcal P_h$ can be arbitrarily close to $1$ as $h$ varies by Chebotarev's theorem.
<!-- end remark-9 -->
